spec.intent:
Worktree /home/lex/workspaces/cratylus-share (branch design/first-share); every path below is under it and no command runs in the main checkout. Census @f2cd7e3a: the design was corrected there; plan architect-position is stopped under `design stability` and its landed architect-role and architect-skills work (7d53132e, e944facb, 9809add3, c076a864, ce240336, 539140df) is this unit's starting state. Re-derive any count or line below if a listed path changed since. Realize the corrected `architect position` in kino's own declarations (packages/canon/src/agents/kino.ts). Operator ruling (note 'named personas and generic positions'): kino, nico and mav are main-session personas, each with its own specialty and personality over the architect role, and each speaks only the architect position; the generic `architect` is the subagent-oriented holder. Holders override scalars and extend sets (packages/canon/src/roles/hold.ts), so what architect-sees-the-design changes in the role reaches them, and what a persona declares itself only its own unit can fix.
THE LOOP (the contract the workflow units of this plan each state their own share of; the shards say what must hold, this is how). (1) The architect cuts a shard and dispatches the planner with it; the planner plans it and, when no plan is bound, binds it, returning only the plan's name. (2) The architect dispatches one integrator for the bound plan, named for the plan and kept warm across its waves where the harness can message a finished delegate (Claude Code: SendMessage to the name given at dispatch; omp: agent messaging); the integrator records each ready unit active as it hands out its address and returns only addresses, `<unit> of <plan>`. (3) The architect dispatches one implementer per address, naming the delegate after the unit and giving it the address and nothing it wrote itself. The implementer reads its spec, builds on its own branch, runs only its unit's own checks, commits its own work, and returns only `landed <unit> of <plan> at <commit>`, or `blocked <unit> of <plan>: spec` when the spec cannot be built as written (the architect routes that address to the planner). Its account of the work stays out of the return; what it doubts or meets beside the path it captures as a note. (4) The architect dispatches the assayer with the address and commit. The assayer reads the shard the unit realizes and the files at that commit, never the spec, and returns the assay verdict: achieved, or not achieved with what is missing in the design's own words, naming the unit and its implementer. (5) Not achieved: the architect sends the findings to the same implementer by the name it gave it, and the unit returns to (4). Achieved: the architect hands the address and commit to the integrator. (6) The integrator combines the unit onto the plan's integration line (a branch cut from main when the plan is bound, `plan/<plan>`) and runs the project's whole check once on the combined tree; no implementer or assayer runs it. Green: it records the unit completed, commits the records written since (plan, design, notes) by pathspec, and returns the unit as whole with the newly ready addresses. Red or a merge conflict: it leaves the line as it was and returns `red <unit> of <plan>: <failing check>`, which the architect sends to the same implementer. It never repairs, never reads to judge, and decides nothing. (7) When every unit is completed and the whole holds, the integrator closes the plan and asks the operator to release the line to main: a pull request where the repository has a forge remote and `gh`, otherwise the exact git command. It never moves main. (8) The architect never runs `plan show <unit>`, and never reads a spec, a diff, an artifact or an implementer's account; it runs no check and makes no commit or merge. Unit names reach it only as addresses, from the integrator and on verdicts. (9) Design stability. Every input, whether from the operator, a delegate or the architect itself, is a hypothesis the architect rectifies against its expertise and industry practice. A surviving change that bears on a shard the bound plan realizes is captured as a decision note on that concept's topic, blocking nothing; it is amended into the design only after that plan closes, and a following plan realizes it. A change to a concept no bound plan realizes is amended at once. Only when the architect finds the bound plan built on a shard that is itself wrong does it stop the plan: it captures a note blocking the plan (an owed ruling, so no unit is ready), corrects the shard once, and the planner rectifies the plan (repin, revise, retract, add) or rebuilds it; the architect then retracts the note and work resumes.
CHANGE. The description ('delegating every mechanical build to subagents, and judging their output against that vision') and the archetype ('keeps the vision whole by delegating every mechanical build to subagents and refusing the output that diverges from it') have kino judge and refuse output itself. They become kino holding the film vision as the design, rectifying the operator's utterances against industry practice (its existing stance, which the corrected position now states for every architect), cutting shards for the planner, and routing assay verdicts, with planning, building, judging a unit against its shard, and making approved work whole handed to planner, implementer, assayer and integrator. The comment at 24-26 gives 'image and video to judge a take' as why `modalities` stays unstated; restate the reason without kino judging an artifact (the operator's references and intent arrive as image, video and audio), or state the value if no other reason holds. Keep the two capabilities, provenance-attribution and user-centered. .changeset/kino-position.md (@cratylus/canon patch). No new test file.

COLD READ. For each of kino, give its session text (RIG), with no other context and no tools, to anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 and anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 with this prompt verbatim: 'Below is the complete definition of an AI agent and the skills loaded into it at session start. Answer from this text alone, quoting the lines that decide each answer, with YES, NO or UNCLEAR where a question asks yes or no. (a) Does it itself build or edit product code or files, other than its own design records? (b) Does it itself run code, tests, builds or checks? (c) Does it itself commit or merge? (d) Does it itself read a unit's spec, a diff, a produced artifact, or an implementer's account of its work? (e) Does it itself decide whether a unit achieves what it was built for? (f) When the verdict on a unit comes back not achieved, what does it do and to whom? And when achieved? (g) While a plan is running, the operator asks for a change to something that plan is building. What does it do? (h) To whom, by name, does it hand planning, building, judging a unit against its goal, and combining approved work and running the full check?' Save every prompt and answer verbatim under /tmp/corrected-shards-cold-read/kino-position/ and print the number of reads taken. PASSES when every read answers NO to (a) through (e); every (f) says not-achieved goes back to the same implementer with the findings and achieved goes to the integrator; every (g) says the change is weighed (rectified) and then waits to be realized by a following plan rather than amending what the running plan builds, unless the goal itself is wrong; every (h) names planner, implementer, assayer and integrator. A YES or UNCLEAR quoting a line this unit's outputs project fails it. FAILS at census: Haiku answered (d) YES ('reads artifacts to judge them against vision') and both Opus reads answered YES to reading output, quoting 'judging their output against that vision … refusing the output that diverges from it' (assay of 20961057).
